thesis: Complexity requires separate accounting of information, memory, discovery, computation and fidelity.

ideas.statement: Short instructions can hide huge tables or precision; account for model and data under declared coding conventions.
Nondominated cost and error vectors form a task-dependent cost–fidelity frontier rather than one universal ranking.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: A compact random law need not compress each realized sequence.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: Best found program length is only an upper bound; state count, entropy, implementation size and energy are distinct.

audit.notes: Complete batch read; headings and navigation excluded from idea ranking.
